fillReport.subOne: {{count}} game was skipped and the run continued.

fillReport.titleSwept: What this run changed on your card
fillReport.hint: The cover is written next to the ROM. These folders are read-only, so it couldn't be created there. Make them writable (e.g. chmod -R u+w) and run again.
fillReport.hintManual: These manuals could not be installed on the card. A download failure is usually temporary — try again; "Not published" means the GameDB lists the manual but has no ready-made file for it yet.
fillReport.hintSwept: These games had guide slots holding a second copy of a document, or manuals auto-fill itself installed at an earlier sync that the GameDB no longer serves — leftovers of the slot addressing this version fixes. They were deleted so the current documents fit; nothing you added yourself is ever touched. The CSV names the exact slots and which kind each was.
fillReport.hintAdopted: Auto-fill recognized these guide slots by the document type in the `.man` header and rewrote IN PLACE the older copy it had installed itself (proven by the ficha’s own receipt) — nothing was deleted and no slot was duplicated. Slots listed as a possible leftover were NOT touched: they look like an older copy but could not be proven to be one, so they are yours to keep or remove from the guides dialog. The CSV names every slot.
fillReport.hintSlotsFull: All 8 guide slots on these games are taken by files auto-fill cannot prove it installed — so it overwrites none of them, because one could be yours. Open the game, go to Guides and delete whatever you don't want to keep with the trash icon, then run the fill again.
fillReport.hintAsset: These artifacts could not be generated. A download failure is usually temporary — try again; "No source in the GameDB" means there is no image to build it from yet.
fillReport.reasonNoReadyPreview: Preview not ready in the GameDB
fillReport.hintPreview: The GameDB has no ready-made preview for these games yet. Auto-fill never encodes video — the clip comes ready inside the package — so they were skipped. You can build one by hand per game (the "Generate .fmv" button under "Available on GameDB"), which is slow, or wait for the GameDB to publish it.

migrate.aborted: Stopped — {{moved}} files had already been moved.
migrate.ambiguous: {{count}} file(s) match a name that exists as BOTH a Game Boy and a SNES game, so there is no way to tell which one they belong to. Rather than guess, they sit in an _ambiguous folder inside the affected root — here is exactly where each group is:
migrate.ambiguousAlready: {{count}} of them are already in that folder from an earlier run — this run will not touch them.
migrate.ambiguousHint: Rename one of the two games so they can be told apart, then organize again — the files leave _ambiguous on their own.
migrate.ambiguousOnly: Nothing could be moved — the only files left need a name conflict resolved first.
migrate.conflicts: {{count}} file(s) already exist at the destination and will be left where they are.
migrate.emptyDirs: {{count}} empty leftover folder(s) from the old layout will be removed — /sd2snes/info is walked on the way to every asset, so dead entries cost every lookup.
migrate.fwAbsent: No firmware.im3 on the card — cannot tell which layout it needs.
migrate.fwAssumedNew: You said this card runs firmware 2.15 or newer, so the new layout is in use.
migrate.fwAssumedOld: You said this card runs firmware 2.14 or older, so the old layout is in use.
migrate.fwSnapshot: Development build on the card ({{version}}) — cannot tell which layout it needs.
migrate.fwOfficial: The stock sd2snes/FXPak firmware is on this card ({{version}}) — it uses neither of this fork’s folder schemes, and it is often just the image left behind after a USB flash. Answer below which firmware the console actually runs.
migrate.fwTooOld: This card's firmware does not read the new folders yet, so nothing will be moved — the console would stop finding your saves. Update the firmware to 2.15 or later first. Removing the system leftovers is safe and still available.
migrate.fwUnknown: Could not read the firmware version from the card.
migrate.junkHint: ._, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini and .crswap files — pure noise, but the console scans them
migrate.noCard: No card connected — connect a card or folder to check its layout.
migrate.noNativeMove: This browser has no fast move, so files are copied one by one — it will take longer. Chrome is quicker.
migrate.nothingToDo: Nothing to do — the card is already organized.
migrate.patchesHint: Firmware 2.15+ skips a patch named exactly like its ROM — that is the shape "Create patched ROM" leaves behind, and re-applying it would corrupt the copy. Renaming puts the patch back in the console's list.
migrate.resAborted: Stopped before the end — what was already moved is in the right place. Organize again to finish.
migrate.resConflicts: {{count}} files left where they were — the destination already had a file with that name
migrate.resJunkFailed: {{count}} leftovers the card would not let us delete — most likely a read-only folder
migrate.resMoved: {{count}} files moved into the new folders
migrate.resPruned: {{count}} empty folders from the old layout removed
migrate.resRemaining: {{count}} files still need moving. Organize again to finish.
migrate.resRenamed: {{count}} patches renamed and back in the console's list
migrate.resSysDirsFailed: {{count}} system folders the browser would not delete — everything else was done
migrate.resUnwritable: The card stopped accepting writes partway through — it may be full, write-protected, or remounted read-only. Nothing was lost: re-seat the card and organize again to finish.
migrate.safetyNote: Files are moved, never copied or overwritten. Nothing is deleted except the macOS leftovers.
migrate.subtitle: New folder layout for firmware 2.15 and later
migrate.sysDirs: Remove system folders (recycle bins and volume metadata)
migrate.sysDirsHint: Off by default on purpose: $RECYCLE.BIN can still hold files you think you have. Ticked, they are deleted whole — contents included. Windows sometimes refuses System Volume Information; if it does, that one stays and the rest of the run carries on.
migrate.title: Organize the card
migrate.unwritable: The card stopped accepting writes after {{moved}} files — it may be full, write-protected, or have been remounted read-only. Nothing was lost: files are moved one at a time. Re-seat the card and organize again to finish. ({{error}})
migrate.warn: This card still uses the old layout, but the firmware on it is 2.15 or later, which only reads the new one. Your saves, cheats and covers are still on the card — the console just is not looking where they are. Organizing puts them back in view. Game Boy games also move into their own sgb folder, so a .gb and a .sfc with the same name stop sharing one save.
migrate.warnPartial: This card is already on the new layout, but {{count}} files are still in the wrong place — the console will not find them there. They are usually saves and covers for Game Boy games, which now live in their own sgb folder so a .gb and a .sfc with the same name stop sharing one save. Organizing puts each one where it belongs.
migrate.why: Firmware 2.15+ groups files into two-letter folders so the console finds them faster. Organizing also removes the macOS ._ files, which double every folder scan. Game Boy games get their own sgb folder inside each of those, so a .gb and a .sfc with the same name stop sharing one save.
